newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end firm on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end firm on foreign buying.

text.p: After a slow start, Chilean stocks rallied midday to close over one percent higher on a wave of foreign orders, especially for power stocks, said dealers.
The bourse is seen opening cautiously as investors await the outcome of the Federal Reserve meeting which ends Wednesday.
"There's a lot of speculation...but most people are expecting good news from the Fed," said one dealer, adding that the market believed the Federal Reserve would leave U.S. interest rates unchanged.
The blue chip IPSA index ended up 1.57 percent at 133.62 points.
The general IGPA index closed 0.64 percent firmer at 5,768.92 points.
Turnover swelled to 12.2 billion pesos from a thin eight billion pesos Monday.
Analysts said Tuesday's rise, the strongest daily rally in weeks, reflected optimism among foreign investors that the bolsa would soon resume its upward swing.
"There's a lot of upside left for the market as corporate 1998 earnings growth will be significant," said Pablo Salcedo, head of research at ING Barings.
Losers included pulp producer Copec, down 2.1 percent at 2,095 pesos and Banco Edwards which shed 1.92 percent at 51 pesos.
ING Barings' forecasts show company earnings are likely to rise an average 28 percent next year, said Salcedo.
Chilean ADRs swung higher on the back of Wall Street's rally with Endesa and Enersis among top gainers.
Traders attributed the interest in power stocks to optimism over the companies' plans for regional expansion and the end of the drought which hit companies' first half earnings.
Endesa ended up 2.09 percent at 317 pesos, while Enersis firmed 2.96 percent to 296 pesos. ((-- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595x212))
